answer:
Headline results of agent run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (source: `python3 ~/poro/agent/report.py <run>`, read-only; no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

- Records analysed: 759 (stride 20, 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314 % of time)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016)

CALIBRATED (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5 — this is the calibrated probability, from the LBNL catalogue):
- b = 1.0:  Sigma -5.449, P(M>=5.5)/yr 0.0001198, P(M>=5.5) in observed volume 5.236e-06, P(M>=3)/yr 0.03719
- b = 0.73: Sigma -5.319, P(M>=5.5)/yr 0.004922,  P(M>=5.5) in observed volume 0.0002155,  P(M>=3)/yr 0.2809
- b = 0.65: Sigma -5.281, P(M>=5.5)/yr 0.01474,   P(M>=5.5) in observed volume 0.0006484,  P(M>=3)/yr 0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
- b = 0.9849, Sigma -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated catalogue-based probabilities (LBNL/NCEDC events, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5) indicate a very low annual probability of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event at Brady Hot Springs during March 2016 (1.2e-4/yr at b=1.0, up to 1.47e-2/yr at b=0.65). The DAS-based number (0.078/yr at b=0.9849) is an upper bound only, because DAS magnitudes are uncalibrated and every detection is counted as an event at or above Mc, so it over-counts and is not calibrated.
